about: Every dashboard of the Nicholls State Institutional Research remodel, ranked by polish and impact. Public ones are embedded live from Tableau Public; internal ones are shown only through sample-data copies; the Dashboard Catalog as screenshots. See README.md.

scores.polish: How finished it is: K's final pass done, nothing cut off, consistent with the rest (1-5).
scores.impact: How much it shows off: the problem it solves, the interaction, how it looks (1-5).

dashboards.title: Market Analysis
dashboards.audience: Public: Nicholls' Tableau Public profile
dashboards.pitch: Every Louisiana parish's college-bound freshmen on one map, with Nicholls' share and how it moved against last year.
dashboards.what_it_shows: Where first-time freshmen from each Louisiana parish go to college and in what program, with trends by system and school.
what_changed: Rebuilt from mockups: parish pies on a Louisiana map at the left; at the right two at-a-glance lists (the state, then the 8-parish region) with green and red arrows for the change from last year.
Click a parish, or any slice of its pie, and a program (CIP) list opens in place of the figures, focused on that parish; Close brings the figures back.
Each school is a shade of its system's color, biggest school darkest; the 8-parish service region in grey on the map.
Four pages under one header (Overview, CIP Detail, System Trend, School Trend), with an academic-year stepper on each. Counts under 5 read "<5".
techniques: Map with pie marks per parish
Dynamic zone visibility (a panel that swaps in)

dashboards.title: Registration Trend
dashboards.audience: Public: Nicholls' Tableau Public profile
dashboards.pitch: Are we ahead of last year? Registration day by day against last year's pace, for the whole university or one class, group or college.
dashboards.what_it_shows: Day-by-day registration leading up to the stat day, against the same point last year, by student group and college.
what_changed: Two columns on every page: an at-a-glance list (registered so far, the same point last year, the change, the share of last year's stat-day total) beside the year comparison.
Dots on stems under each comparison show how far ahead (blue) or behind (orange) last year each weekday was; K chose this from a set of mockups.
Steppers for year, term, college and student group; the selected year red, last year grey.
Five pages: Overall, Class, Group, College, Compare.

dashboards.title: Admissions Dashboard
dashboards.audience: Public: Nicholls' Tableau Public profile
dashboards.pitch: The admissions funnel at a glance: applied, accepted and enrolled, each fall measured against the one before.
dashboards.what_it_shows: How many students apply, are accepted and enroll, term by term and by student population.
what_changed: Key figures named by the fall ("Fall 2026", "vs Fall 2025") with signed changes; the pattern every other dashboard took up.
Funnel stages in brand colors; admissions by student type on a true dual axis; a trend page.
New Departments page with full department names.
Filters moved off the page into a Filters box, with one line under the header saying what the page is filtered to.

dashboards.title: Overall Enrollment
dashboards.audience: Public: shown on the IR office's website
dashboards.pitch: The whole student body on one screen: eight breakdowns, each with last year's figure and the change in its tooltip.
dashboards.what_it_shows: The student body at the start of each term: classification, level, college, department, program, race, gender, residency and delivery, with term-by-term trends.
what_changed: Breakdown page as an even grid of tiles; pies became labeled bars; a new dual-enrollment chart.
Every tooltip compares with the same term a year earlier ("vs Fall 2025: +56 (+4.5%)").
By Program: at-a-glance figures, the six biggest gains and drops, and every program code shown with its full name (341 codes from 25 years of curriculum lists).
Its college colors became the standard for every dashboard (race and gender follow the same standard).

dashboards.title: Advancement Through Nicholls
dashboards.audience: Public: Nicholls' Tableau Public profile
dashboards.pitch: Follows each entering class year by year, as a flow: who advanced, who did not, who graduated and who left.
dashboards.what_it_shows: Follows each entering group (new freshmen, transfers, readmits, adults) to see who moved up a class level, who didn't, and who left.
what_changed: Colors that tell the story: graduated in Nicholls red, advanced light red, did not advance grey, left light grey.
A heading over each column ("Entered as", "Started", "After 1 year" ... "After 4 years") and readable labels on the bars.
New Outcomes page: the entering class at a glance, where it stood after each year, and every class side by side.
Steppers for the entering class and the student type.

dashboards.title: Dashboard Catalog
dashboards.audience: Internal office catalog: shown here as screenshots
dashboards.pitch: One front door to 35 dashboards: pick an area, see its dashboards as cards, open one in a click.
dashboards.what_it_shows: The office's catalog of its 35 dashboards: nine areas, each with the question it answers and its dashboards as cards, plus an A-to-Z list of what each one shows and where it lives.
what_changed: A tangled relationship diagram became a catalog designed from mockups: areas with icons on the left; cards, or an A-to-Z table, on the right.
An audience stepper (All, Public on Tableau, On the IR website, Internal only) and a Find box; cards the choice leaves out stay in place, greyed.
K's own icons for each dashboard and new area icons, drawn into the workbook; the list itself is a spreadsheet the office edits (name, area, description, order).
dashboards.note: Not embedded: on Tableau Public the catalog's Open buttons lead to the office's internal dashboards. Shown as screenshots. Names and descriptions in the catalog are fine to show.

what_changed: Eight pages under one header with a second row of page buttons (World, States, ZIP Codes, Regions, Public vs Private, By Parish, LA Schools, Athletes).
Maps redrawn: solid fills on a log-scaled light red ramp, so a state with a few students still shows beside Louisiana; smaller slate points so clusters read as clusters.
Fall, athlete and honors steppers; at-a-glance figures and the top sending high schools.
techniques: Filled and point maps at three levels
